description:
The Responsible Business team leads and supports the firm’s environmental management and sustainability strategy (including climate, carbon and resource use), as well as human rights and wider ESG work. The team works closely with other parts of the business to coordinate activity, align environmental and social objectives, and drive measurable, ESG‑led progress.
  
  
Purpose of the Role
  
  
The ESG and Sustainability Manager will play a key role in developing and delivering Simmons & Simmons’ environmental and climate strategy across its global offices, overseeing carbon and climate‑related reporting, environmental management systems, carbon reduction programmes, supplier engagement, and green building and office projects. The role will ensure compliance with evolving ESG, regulatory and market standards and is central to delivering the firm’s Responsible Business Strategy and climate commitments, while meeting client, regulatory and wider stakeholder expectations.
  
  
Key responsibilities
  
  
·
  
  
**Strategy & Reporting:**  
Lead the firm’s environmental and climate strategy, aligned with Responsible Business priorities. Coordinate global carbon reporting, the Climate Transition Plan and related risk/opportunity analysis. Manage key external disclosures including the Carbon Reduction Plan, SBTi requirements, climate‑related financial disclosures (CFD) and CDP, and oversee ISO 14001, ESOS and SECR processes and audits.
  
  
·
  
  
**Governance & Committees:**  
Support with the Responsible Business Board, Climate Committee and The Green Room providing insight on environmental performance, risks an d emerging regulatory developments.
  
  
·
  
  
**Environmental & Carbon Reduction Initiatives:**  
Develop and implement initiatives to reduce operational emissions and broader environmental impacts, including travel-related emissions. Coordinate environmental and sustainability training across the firm where necessary.
  
  
·
  
  
**Sustainable Procurement & Supplier Engagement:**  
Integrate sustainability into procurement and supplier management, working closely with EnterpriseRisk Management (ERM) and related teams. Lead supplier engagement under the SBT Action Plan to reduce Scope 3 emissions, set and communicate environmental expectations and track supplier performance.
  
  
·
  
  
**Offices, Real Estate& Green Buildings:**  
Provide sustainability input into office projects (including25 Finsbury Square) ensuring environmental requirements are built into design and operation. Support the facilities team with green building certifications(e.g. BREEAM, LEED) and improve building energy performance across the global estate.
  
  
·
  
  
**Charters, Memberships & External Commitments:**  
Manage participation in environmental and climate initiatives, such as the Legal 1.5°CCharter and the Legal Sustainability Alliance. Ensure commitments are embedded as part of the responsible business strategy.
  
  
·
  
  
**Horizon Scanning &Regulatory Compliance:**  
Track evolving ESG and environmental regulation and standards and prepare for key obligations (e.g. UK SRS, CSRD and CSDDD). Provide guidance on implications for the firm, and coordinate internal activity to ensure compliance.
  
  
·
  
  
**Policies:**  
Review and update environmental and other relevant policies, and ensure they are clearly communicated.
  
  
·
  
  
**Stakeholder and client support:**  
Oversee environmental and ESG input into RFPs, pitches and panel reviews and coordinate responses to client environmental audits and questionnaires. Where relevant, work with client relationship teams to articulate the firm’s environmental credentials and support client discussions on ESG topics.
  
  
Experience and personal specification
  
  

* Excellent communication, coordination and project management skills.
* Strong knowledge and understanding of ESG and environmental sustainability, including carbon accounting, climate risk, Science Based Targets (SBTi), and environmental management systems (e.g. ISO 14001).
* Experience of supporting environmental, ESG and regulatory reporting processes (e.g. SECR, ESOS, CDP, climate‑related financial disclosures), including data collection, assurance and narrative development.
* Experience setting, monitoring or reporting against KPIs, impact measures or performance indicators.
* Strong writing, editing and content development skills, including drafting clear governance papers, environmental policies, internal reports and client‑facing ESG materials.
* Experience with policy development, review and implementation.
* Confidence working with senior stakeholders, internal committees and cross-functional teams.
* Ability to work independently and make sound decisions in line with the firm’s goals and values.

Simmons & Simmons is a leading international law firm, providing clients with commercially aware legal advice, whenever and wherever they need it. We have over 1,600 people situated in key business and financial centres across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
  
  
We understand that our firm is equal only to the strengths of our people and place great emphasis on recruiting and retaining staff who meet our high standards. Our philosophy for international growth has been to build practices around local teams who understand the culture, business and languages of the countries and regions in which we operate. In doing so, we believe that we have succeeded in developing a closely knit and cohesive network that meets local business needs as part of a global service.
  
  
Our business services groups provide integrated support for our global operations. The firm is organised in line with our clients’ requirements into key practice areas and sector groups. **Company Description**

Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.  
Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.  
Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.  
We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.  
Please visit our website: www.turnerandtownsend.com

 **Job Description**

The Sustainability Manager is responsible for the direct design, execution, and delivery of environmental initiatives across the company's data centre portfolio. This role leads the onsite PMC and operations teams, drives the general contractor’s green progress, and handles day-to-day client interactions to ensure the project lowers its carbon footprint, improves energy efficiency, and meets global green standards.

**Key Responsibilities**

Strategy & Energy Efficiency

* Create the green roadmap: Design and execute the mid- and long-term sustainability plans for data centre locations.
* Improve Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE): Team up with engineers to cut energy use in cooling and power systems.
* Source clean energy: Lead corporate power procurement efforts like Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and renewable energy certificates.

Carbon, Water & Circular Economy

* Track emissions: Manage Scope 1, 2, and 3 carbon accounting across all mission-critical sites.
* Save resources: Create plans to cut Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) and reduce liquid cooling resource drains.
* Reduce waste: Setup zero-waste initiatives and circular recycling pathways for server hardware and batteries.

Compliance & Reporting

* Keep certifications updated: Guide building operations to meet and keep LEED, BREEAM, or Green Mark certifications.
* Write standard disclosures: Produce annual sustainability filings matching GRI, CDP, SASB, and ISSB frameworks.
* Follow local laws: Keep track of changing energy conservation acts and greenhouse gas rules.

  
**Qualifications**

Required Qualifications & Experience

* Education & Professional Credentials
* Degree needed: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related area.
* Preferred certifications: LEED AP, Green Mark Manager, Certified Energy Manager (CEM), other sustainability certifications.

Experience

* Time in field: 8 to 10+ years working directly in sustainability or energy systems management.
* Data centre focus: Strong background working inside data centres, critical infrastructure, or large-scale cloud operations.

Technical Mastery & Sequencing

* System knowledge: Solid understanding of critical data centre layouts, power backup systems, industrial chillers, and regional renewable energy markets.
* Construction logic: Understanding of how to embed energy-saving metrics and resource conservation into the building and operations lifecycle.

Data & Communication Proficiency

* Data skills: Experience building data-driven energy models and emissions calculations using advanced Excel or ESG software.
* Communication: Ability to share complex energy metrics clearly with corporate executives and international clients.
